title: Grate a block of cheese on a box grater onto a cutting board
instruction: Grate the block of cheese on the box grater onto the board. Then put the cheese down, leave the grater standing on the board and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Grating cheese, vegetables or zest is routine kitchen prep. A box grater is light and tall and its teeth bite on every stroke, so the cook holds it by its handle with one hand and grates with the other; unheld, it tips over.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed beech-wood cutting board, 30 cm front to back, 34 cm wide and 1.2 cm thick, centred 30 cm forward and 1 cm right. (2) A loose steel box grater, 180 g, 8 cm front to back, 7 cm wide and 13 cm tall, open at the bottom, standing on the board 30 cm forward on the centre line. Its right side, toward the right arm, is the grating face (from 2 to 11.5 cm up); a black plastic flat handle 10 cm long reaches left from its top. (3) A loose yellow block of cheese, 50 g, 6 cm long, 2.4 cm wide and 3.5 cm tall, lying on the board along the left-right line, its middle 30 cm forward and 14 cm right. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged from the whole trial. The cheese counts as rubbed on the grating face while its end is on the face (within 4 mm of it, inside the grating area, 2 to 11.5 cm up) and the grater stands within 20 degrees of upright; the score counts the cumulative distance the cheese travels up and down the face that way. In the simulation one shred of cheese falls inside the grater for each 2 cm; in a real trial the same distance is measured from video along the face, so 2 cm still equals one simulated shred. 1.0: at least 18 cm rubbed and, at the end, the grater standing on the board (within 20 degrees of upright, its foot on the board inside its edges), the cheese put down (lying on the board or the table, its middle at most 3 cm above the board) and both arms back where they started (each fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: at least 10 cm rubbed (or 18 cm without that end state); 0.25: at least 2 cm rubbed; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the grater, the cheese and the fallen shreds still.
reset_notes: Lift the grater, pick the shreds off the board, stand the grater back on its spot and put the cheese where it lay.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the cheese does not wear down. The score uses the rubbing distance along the face; as a visual cue 12 small rigid shreds are brought in from out of sight, one inside the grater per 2 cm. The teeth's bite is a drag the task file puts on the grater along the stroke (at most 4 N), which tips an unheld grater over. The board is fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
